notes: Ran a 4-card HQ five times a turn on turns 2-3 at 0 credits, eating repeated Increased Drop Rates tags, then spent turns 4-11 in a loop of clicking credits and paying 2 to clear tags, never installing Carmen or the rest of the grip. Facechecked Ping with 1-2 credits and no breaker on turns 7, 9 and 10, and never mounted any pressure while the Corp scored out.

Left Hybrid Release naked in Server 1 overnight on turn 1, and later turns 11-17 were slow at finding the last point (Server 3 card on turn 15 never used). Otherwise it scored efficiently (Hybrid Release on turn 3, Sericulture Expansion on turns 6 and 10) and kept the economy healthy with Hedge Fund and Petty Cash.

Hoarded 48 credits by clicking for credits nearly every turn from turn 3 on and never installed a second breaker with five cards in the grip. Ignored advancing remotes on turn 9 (Server 2, Above the Law) and turn 17 (Server 1, final Divested Trust, Corp nearly broke), and ran Server 1 into Envelopment on turn 14 with no answer for it.

Rezzing Ansel 1.0 early on turn 3 locked down HQ and Server 1, protecting Superconducting Hub and Méliès City Luxury Line, and the Corp scored Project Ingatan in one turn (turn 6) plus two Méliès. Minor oddities: rezzing a second Wage Workers on turn 8 trashed the first, and it spent several turns clicking for credits from near zero.

Kept running R&D into rezzed Piranhas on turns 6, 8, 9, 11 and 16 with no way to break it, losing Bravado, Daily Casts, Masterwork and more to net damage. The economy stayed at 0-5 credits all game, so it never contested Server 1, where Freedom of Information and Witch Hunt were advanced, even when the Corp was at 0 credits on turns 15-16.

Installed Nico Campaign naked twice (turn 6 Server 3, turn 10 Server 5) and both were trashed. R&D was left behind a single Vertigo that Cat's Cradle broke for 1, letting the Runner steal Megaprix Qualifier and Architect Deployment Test. Scoring was decent (Seamless Launch for Project Ingatan on turn 4, Méliès to win), but credits sat at 0 most turns.

Efficient aggression: Into the Depths runs stole Next Big Thing and Remastered Edition on turn 2, and it correctly ignored tags while the Corp was broke. On turn 4 it took the winning steal from Server 1 against a Corp with 0 credits; installing Unity first was harmless.

Clicked for credits up to 55 while holding five unplayed cards. It let Above the Law score from Server 2 (turns 4-5) and Server 3 (turns 7-8) uncontested, then sat idle on turns 22-25 at 6 points with 40+ credits instead of running HQ/R&D. It gave up on the final Server 7 Divested Trust after one bounce off Tree Line on turn 26.

No economy (1-5 credits all game), so HQ ice was never rezzed and the Runner walked into HQ for Hybrid Release, Lotus Haze and Sisyphus Protocol on turns 4 and 6. Lotus Haze was stolen from Server 1 on turn 3 because the outer ice was never rezzed. Turn 5 spent clicks icing the two Mavirus servers instead of fixing credits or HQ.

Good trap play: advanced Urtica Cipher bluffs in Server 1 and Server 3, Saisentan on HQ, and a double Anemone remote on turn 11 that flatlined the Runner. Weak spots were leaving R&D ice unrezzed (Lotus Haze stolen on turn 5) and a thin economy with several click-for-credit turns.

Slow start, clicking for credits on turns 2-5 with 8-10 credits and few installs, and Spin Doctor was put naked on turn 5 and trashed. Afterwards it scored steadily behind Mestnichestvo and Ping (Tomorrow's Headline turn 12, Embedded Reporting turn 13, Post-Truth Dividend turn 14, Next Big Thing turn 19).

Coherent R&D lock: Banner got through Akhet every turn and won on accesses. Small inefficiencies: drawing into a full grip and discarding (turns 1, 5, 10), Gachapon on turn 4 removing two Sure Gambles from the game, and never spending the stacked Leech counters.

Played Oppo Research on turns 5 and 6 (paying 5 extra for 4 tags) with no follow-up to punish the tags. HQ and R&D were protected only by Ping and the swapped Mestnichestvo, so Embedded Reporting and Tomorrow's Headline were stolen from centrals. Remote scoring of Tomorrow's Headline and Next Big Thing was fine, but the last Server 1 agenda was run with a big Runner credit pool against it.

Repeatedly ran Server 3, took Anemone's single net damage, then jacked out before accessing (turns 4, 5, 7 twice, 11 twice), letting all three Longevity Serums score, including the game-winner on turn 12. It also sat idle on turns 8-9 with 13-18 credits and reinstalled a second Pennyshaver on turn 10, which was immediately trashed.

Solid tempo: broke Anemone with Revolver for a turn 3 Longevity Serum steal, used Carpe Diem on Archives for Fujii Asset Retrieval on turn 5, and on turn 6 hit HQ then Jailbreak on R&D to win. Minor issue: a no-breaker facecheck of Tatu-Bola on Server 1 at 3 credits on turn 4, which let Project Yagi-Uda score.

Built a four-ice Server 1 but never installed an agenda in it. From turn 8 to 16 it only clicked for credits (up to 26), discarding at end of turn, while HQ held Megaprix Qualifier, two Architect Deployment Tests and Project Ingatan behind a single Hagen. The Runner swept them all on turn 16.

Sensible plan: built economy, then used Banner to get through the Akhets on HQ and R&D for steady steals, finishing with SDS Drone Deployment on turn 11. Minor oddities: a slow setup on turns 2-5 and Archives runs on turns 8-10 that gained little.

Kept advancing and stacking ice on the already-accessed Urtica Cipher in Server 1 (turns 3-5), then from turns 16-20 spent every turn at 0 credits paying 2 to trash Cookbook instead of rebuilding. Being broke left HQ ice unrezzable, so Project Yagi-Uda was stolen from HQ on turn 20 and Sericulture Expansion from a one-ice Server 3 on turn 21.

Won with a Seamless Launch/Ansel 1.0 scoring remote (Project Ingatan, Architect Deployment Test, Superconducting Hub, Méliès) while Ansel stopped every steal. It lost Megaprix Qualifier x2 and Architect Deployment Test from HQ early and over-built its economy to 59 credits with idle draw clicks on turns 6-9.

Good early steals (Next Big Thing turn 1, Remastered Edition turn 5, Oracle Thinktank turns 6 and 14), but ran an unchanged R&D four times on both turns 2 and 3, re-seeing the same top card. It also spent turns 7, 9, 10 and 11 clicking for credits with 13-25 credits and a full grip instead of pressuring HQ or R&D.
